items.title: 法國至少3,000家商鋪遭劫掠 巴黎等多城局部宵禁
items.title_en: France sees at least 3,000 shops looted, partial curfews imposed in Paris and other cities
paras: 法國巴黎等多座城市19日（周一）夜間至20日凌晨局部宵禁，以防騷亂重演。巴黎共和國廣場和萊阿勒購物中心17日發生嚴重打砸搶燒事件，被列入宵禁範圍。
此外，巴黎警察局宣布部分地區禁止集會。
法國東南部城市里昂、北部城市里爾、南部海濱城市尼斯等地也宣布局部宵禁，其中里爾和尼斯的宵禁只適用於未成年人。法國第二大城市馬賽19日12時至20時禁止一切公共集會或示威活動。
法國17日爆發全國性示威，遍及巴黎、里昂、里爾、馬賽、波爾多、斯特拉斯堡等多座城市。法國政府估計，全國約55萬人參加示威，組織方則稱人數達到80萬。
部分城市的示威活動演變為暴力衝突。巴黎多處出現焚燒車輛、打砸商鋪等亂象，里昂旅遊局一分支機構當天遭縱火和搶劫，馬賽、里爾的市政廳遭抗議者闖入和破壞。
據政府統計，法國全國至少3,000家商鋪遭劫掠。
部分工會和學生組織將下一次全國性抗議日期定在11月5日。參與17日示威的部分活動人士稱，會在10月24日再次舉行示威。
中國駐法國使領館19日再次提醒公民提高風險防範意識，密切關注當地形勢，遠離遊行示威地區。
paras_en: On the night of the 19th (Monday) through the early hours of the 20th, several French cities including Paris imposed partial curfews to prevent a repeat of the riots. The Republic Square and the La Défense shopping centre in Paris, which suffered severe smash‑and‑grab and arson incidents on the 17th, were placed within the curfew zones.
In addition, the Paris police announced a ban on gatherings in certain districts.

Cities in southeastern France such as Lyon, northern cities like Lille, and the southern coastal city of Nice also declared partial curfews, with the restrictions in Lille and Nice applying only to minors. Marseille, France’s second‑largest city, prohibited all public assemblies or demonstrations from 12:00 to 20:00 on the 19th.

A nationwide protest erupted on the 17th, spreading across Paris, Lyon, Lille, Marseille, Bordeaux, Strasbourg and other cities. The French government estimates that about 550,000 people took part nationwide, while organizers claim the figure reached 800,000.

In some cities the protests turned violent. Paris saw numerous incidents of vehicle burning and shop vandalism; a branch of the Lyon tourism office was set on fire and robbed; and municipal buildings in Marseille and Lille were breached and damaged by protesters.
According to government statistics, at least 3,000 shops across France were looted.
Some unions and student groups have scheduled the next nationwide protest for November 5, while participants in the 17th demonstrations said another rally would be held on October 24.
The Chinese embassy in France on the 19th again urged its citizens to heighten risk awareness, closely monitor the local situation, and stay away from areas of protests and demonstrations.

items.title: 黃仁勳週三登場！輝達GTC五大看點曝光 能否成AI股反攻關鍵？
items.title_en: Jensen Huang Takes the Stage on Wednesday! Nvidia GTC's Five Key Themes Unveiled – A Crucial Test for AI Stock Rally
paras: AI產業上週接連遭遇市場考驗，AI投資邏輯正面臨一輪罕見的壓力測試。在此背景下，輝達(Nvidia)(NVDA-US)即將舉行的GTC大會，或將為觀察下一階段AI產業的發展方向提供重要線索。
NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026將於當地時間10月20日至22日在德國柏林舉行。輝達CEO黃仁勳將於台灣時間10月21日17:00至19:00發表主題演講，分享對AI技術與產業發展的最新展望。與其單純關注是否推出新產品，市場更值得留意的是：當AI投資進入回報驗證階段，輝達將如何進一步拓展AI基建需求、推動AI代理實施，以及將AI能力延伸至工業與物理世界。
AI投資進入驗證期，GTC為何備受關注？
過去幾年，AI產業的投資主線相對清晰：大模型能力持續提升，推動算力需求增長，進而帶動GPU、伺服器、網絡設備及資料中心等環節的資本開支。
但隨著AI基建投入不斷擴大，市場關注點正在發生變化。
首先，算力需求增長，不等於所有算力投資都能獲得理想回報。 資料中心建設涉及晶片採購、電力供應、網絡設備及融資成本，只有當企業能夠持續獲得客戶需求、提高算力利用率並實現商業化，巨額投入才有望形成可持續的收益。
其次，AI應用正從模型訓練走向推理與實際部署。企業不再只關注模型能力，也開始重視推理成本、運行效率、數據安全，以及AI能否真正融入業務流程。
因此，本次GTC的重要觀察重點，是輝達如何完善從晶片、系統、軟體到應用的AI生態，以及這些技術進展能否創造新的需求。
五大主題浮現，AI產業下一站看哪裡？
從本次GTC Berlin公布的議程來看，大會不僅聚焦算力基建，還將涉及主權AI與企業AI、AI原生企業、AI安全、AI工廠，以及物理AI等方向。
1. 主權AI與企業AI：AI基建需求能否進一步擴大？
在主權AI與企業AI環節，討論重點是各國及企業如何利用自身數據、行業知識與基礎設施，建設並部署自己的AI能力。嘉賓包括達梭系統CEO Pascal Daloz、德國電信CEO Tim Höttges，以及Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch。
AI需求不再只來自少數大型模型公司。政府、電信運營商、工業企業及其他大型機構，也可能因數據主權、合規要求及業務效率而建設專屬AI系統。
若企業級AI部署持續擴大，算力基建、私有化部署、企業級軟體及數據安全等領域，都有望獲得新的需求。
2. AI原生企業：AI能否從技術突破走向商業增長？
AI原生企業環節將探討歐洲創業者與投資者如何利用AI技術，打造新一代企業。相關嘉賓包括Corti.AI聯合創辦人Andreas Cleve、General Catalyst的Jeannette zu Fürstenberg、Black Forest Labs共同創辦人Robin Rombach，以及Ineffable Intelligence創辦人David Silver。
這項環節的重點在於AI應用的商業化進展。 如果AI不再只是提升既有軟體的效率，而是能夠催生新的產品、服務及商業模式，AI產業的增長來源便有望從基礎設施投資，進一步延伸至應用與服務收入。
不過，客戶付費意願、收入增長及盈利能力，仍是驗證商業模式能否成立的關鍵。
3. AI安全與企業級部署：代理實施還缺什麼？
隨著AI Agent逐步具備調用工具、存取數據及執行任務的能力，安全問題也變得更加重要。本次相關環節邀請CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz、Hugging Face創辦人Thomas Wolf，以及Red Hat的Chris Wright參與討論。
當AI從回答問題轉向執行任務，企業必須確保AI能夠在授權範圍內存取數據、執行操作，並具備可靠的安全防護機制。
因此，AI代理的普及不僅涉及模型能力，也涉及身份驗證、權限管理、網絡安全及企業軟體架構。AI安全與企業級軟體能否創造更多商業價值，將取決於實際部署規模與客戶需求。
4. AI工廠：算力基建的競爭將走向系統效率
AI工廠是本次GTC的另一項重要議題，相關討論將聚焦如何透過基礎設施建設，提高生產效率並帶動經濟增長。代表嘉賓包括施耐德電氣的Frédéric Godemel、Brookfield 的Siko Rashid，以及NEBIUS 創辦人兼CEO Arkady Volozh。
AI工廠並不只是採購GPU，而是涵蓋運算、網絡、記憶體、供電、散熱及軟體調度的完整系統。
當AI集群規模持續擴大，單一晶片的性能已不足以決定整體效率。如何提高集群利用率、降低每單位運算成本，以及縮短資料中心部署週期，都將影響算力投資的回報。
因此，除了GPU需求，高速互連、網絡設備、電力及資料中心基建等環節也值得關注。
5. 物理AI與工業AI：AI將走出資料中心
Physical AI，即物理AI，將AI能力延伸至機器人、汽車及工業設備等真實世界場景。本次相關環節的嘉賓包括Agile Robots的陳兆鵬（Zhaopeng Chen）、西門子醫療的Arthur Kaindl、賓士 CEO Ola Källenius，以及Humanoid的Artem Sokolov。
與主要處理文字、圖像及數據的生成式AI不同，Physical AI需要理解物理環境，並透過感知、推理、模擬及控制，完成現實世界中的任務。
這一方向有望將AI需求延伸至機器人、工業自動化、智慧汽車及相關運算平台。
不過，從技術展示走向規模化商業部署仍有距離。機器人的實際作業能力、成本、可靠性及客戶採用速度，才是判斷產業能否持續增長的關鍵。
投資觀察重點
綜合本次大會議程，市場可以重點觀察以下三個方向：
第一，算力需求能否持續擴張。 除了輝達的晶片與系統布局，企業級AI、主權AI及AI工廠是否帶來新的基建需求，也將影響產業鏈的成長空間。
第二，AI代理能否創造實際商業價值。 若AI逐步從輔助工具走向自主執行任務，推理運算、安全軟體及企業級部署可能獲得更多機會，但仍需驗證成本與收入之間的關係。
第三，物理AI能否開啟新的增長空間。 機器人、工業自動化及智慧汽車等場景，可能拓寬AI的應用邊界，但商業化速度與盈利模式仍有待觀察。
需要注意的是，GTC是技術與產業交流的重要窗口，並不意味著大會上的每一項技術進展都會立即轉化為企業收入或股價催化。
在AI投資邏輯面臨重新評估之際，真正決定產業長期走勢的，仍是算力需求能否持續、資本開支能否獲得回報，以及AI應用能否形成可持續的商業模式。
paras_en: AI industry faced market tests last week, putting AI investment logic under rare pressure. Against this backdrop, Nvidia's (NVDA-US) upcoming GTC conference could provide key clues about the next phase of AI development.

NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 will be held in Berlin, Germany from October 20‑22 local time. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will deliver a keynote from 17:00‑19:00 Taiwan time on October 21, sharing the latest outlook on AI technology and industry development. Beyond new product launches, the market should watch how Nvidia expands AI infrastructure demand, drives AI agent deployment, and extends AI capabilities to industrial and physical worlds as AI investment moves into a return‑validation stage.
Why is GTC drawing attention as AI investment enters the validation phase?

In recent years the main investment theme in AI has been clear: larger model capabilities drive higher compute demand, which in turn fuels capital spending on GPUs, servers, networking gear and data‑center infrastructure.
But as AI infrastructure spending keeps expanding, market focus is shifting.

First, growing compute demand does not guarantee that every compute investment will yield ideal returns. Data‑center builds involve chip purchases, power supply, networking equipment and financing costs; only when companies can sustain customer demand, improve compute utilization and commercialize the technology will massive outlays translate into sustainable earnings.

Second, AI applications are moving from model training to inference and real‑world deployment. Enterprises are no longer only concerned with model capability; they also care about inference cost, operational efficiency, data security, and whether AI can truly integrate into business processes.
Thus the key observation at this GTC is how Nvidia will refine the AI ecosystem—from chips and systems to software and applications—and whether these advances can generate new demand.
Five major themes emerge – where is the AI industry headed next?

The Berlin GTC agenda shows the conference will not only focus on compute infrastructure but also cover sovereign AI and enterprise AI, AI‑native enterprises, AI safety, AI factories, and physical AI.
1. Sovereign AI and Enterprise AI: Can AI infrastructure demand expand further?

In the sovereign and enterprise AI track, the discussion centers on how nations and companies can use their own data, industry knowledge and infrastructure to build and deploy their own AI capabilities. Guests include Dassault Systèmes CEO Pascal Daloz, Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges, and Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch.

AI demand is no longer limited to a few large‑model firms. Governments, telecom operators, industrial firms and other large institutions may also build dedicated AI systems for data‑sovereignty, compliance and efficiency reasons.
If enterprise‑level AI deployments keep growing, compute infrastructure, private‑cloud deployments, enterprise software and data‑security segments are likely to see fresh demand.
2. AI‑Native Enterprises: Can AI move from technical breakthroughs to commercial growth?

The AI‑native enterprise session will explore how European founders and investors are leveraging AI to create the next generation of companies. Speakers include Corti.AI co‑founder Andreas Cleve, General Catalyst’s Jeannette zu Fürstenberg, Black Forest Labs co‑founder Robin Rombach, and Ineffable Intelligence founder David Silver.

The focus here is the commercialization of AI applications. If AI can do more than boost existing software efficiency—by spawning new products, services and business models—growth can shift from pure infrastructure spending to revenue from applications and services.
Nevertheless, customer willingness to pay, revenue growth and profitability remain the litmus tests for any business model.
3. AI Safety and Enterprise‑Scale Deployment: What’s still missing for agent implementation?

As AI agents gain the ability to call tools, access data and execute tasks, security concerns become paramount. This segment features CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz, Hugging Face founder Thomas Wolf, and Red Hat’s Chris Wright.
When AI moves from answering questions to performing tasks, enterprises must ensure agents can access data and act only within authorized bounds, backed by robust security safeguards.

Thus the spread of AI agents involves not just model capability but also authentication, permission management, cyber‑security and enterprise software architecture. Whether AI safety and enterprise software can create added commercial value will depend on deployment scale and customer needs.
4. AI Factories: Compute infrastructure competition will shift toward system efficiency

AI factories are another key GTC topic, focusing on how infrastructure builds can boost production efficiency and drive economic growth. Speakers include Schneider Electric’s Frédéric Godemel, Brookfield’s Siko Rashid, and NEBIUS founder‑CEO Arkady Volozh.
An AI factory is more than buying GPUs; it encompasses compute, networking, memory, power, cooling and software scheduling as an integrated system.

As AI cluster sizes keep growing, the performance of a single chip no longer determines overall efficiency. Improving cluster utilization, lowering per‑unit compute cost and shortening data‑center deployment cycles will all affect compute investment returns.
Therefore, beyond GPU demand, high‑speed interconnects, networking gear, power and data‑center construction merit close attention.
5. Physical AI and Industrial AI: AI Leaving the Data Center

Physical AI extends AI capabilities to robots, cars and industrial equipment in real‑world settings. Speakers include Agile Robots’ Zhaopeng Chen, Siemens Healthineers’ Arthur Kaindl, Mercedes‑Benz CEO Ola Källenius, and Humanoid’s Artem Sokolov.

Unlike generative AI that mainly handles text, images and data, Physical AI must understand the physical environment and use perception, reasoning, simulation and control to accomplish real‑world tasks.
This direction could push AI demand into robotics, industrial automation, smart vehicles and related compute platforms.

However, moving from tech demos to scaled commercial deployment still has a way to go. The actual operational capability, cost, reliability and adoption speed of robots will determine whether the sector can sustain growth.
Investment Observation Points
Based on the conference agenda, the market can focus on three key areas:

First, whether compute demand can keep expanding. In addition to Nvidia’s chip and system roadmap, enterprise AI, sovereign AI and AI factories could generate new infrastructure demand, influencing the industry‑chain growth horizon.

Second, whether AI agents can create real commercial value. If agents evolve from assistance tools to autonomous task executors, inference compute, security software and enterprise‑scale deployments may see more opportunities, though the cost‑revenue relationship still needs validation.

Third, whether physical AI can open new growth space. Robotics, industrial automation and smart‑vehicle scenarios could broaden AI’s application frontier, but commercialization speed and viable profit models remain to be seen.

It’s worth noting that GTC is an important venue for technology and industry exchange, but not every technical advance presented will instantly translate into corporate revenue or stock‑price catalysts.

As AI investment logic is re‑evaluated, the long‑term trajectory of the industry will still hinge on whether compute demand remains sustainable, capital spending yields returns, and AI applications can form enduring business models.

items.title: 以色列總理下令 推翻伊朗政權
items.title_en: Israeli Prime Minister Orders Overthrow of Iranian Regime
paras: 以色列總理尼坦雅胡19日（周一）晚在接受以色列第14頻道電視台採訪時說，他向以軍、以色列情報和特勤局（摩薩德）以及以軍軍事情報局下達了「推翻伊朗政權」的指令。
尼坦雅胡表示，美國總統川普的態度「非常明確」，即認為當前「核心任務是徹底消除伊朗對以色列造成的生存威脅 」。
此外，伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊發言人莫赫比19日放話：「荷姆茲海峽下方鋪設了7條主要電纜，全球網路與商業資料都仰賴這些電纜。我方提醒這一點，就是要讓敵人知道。」
這番言論並未明確宣布將攻擊電纜，但在荷姆茲海峽航運持續受阻、美國試圖護送油輪通行之際，為中東通訊安全增添新的不確定性。
不過，電信研究機構 TeleGeography 指出，荷姆茲海峽的海底電纜主要為波斯灣國家提供服務。若電纜遭破壞，可能嚴重干擾區域通訊，但這些破壞對歐洲與亞洲之間的資料傳輸影響相對有限，與伊朗所稱全球網路均仰賴這些電纜的說法有落差。
paras_en: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu said on Monday evening, October 19, in an interview with Israel’s Channel 14 television, that he has issued orders to the Israeli Defense Forces, intelligence services, the Mossad and the military intelligence directorate to "overthrow the Iranian regime."
Netanyahu added that U.S. President Trump’s stance is "very clear," viewing the current "core mission" as the complete elimination of the existential threat Iran poses to Israel.

In addition, IRGC spokesperson Mohbi said on the 19th that seven major cables have been laid beneath the Hormuz Strait, and that the global internet and commercial data rely on these cables, warning the enemy of this fact.

While the statement did not explicitly announce an attack on the cables, it adds new uncertainty to Middle‑East communications security as shipping in the Hormuz Strait remains disrupted and the United States attempts to escort tankers through the passage.

TeleGeography, a telecom research firm, notes that the subsea cables in the Hormuz Strait primarily serve Gulf countries; damage to them could severely disrupt regional communications, but would have relatively limited impact on data traffic between Europe and Asia, contrary to Iran’s claim that the world’s internet depends on those cables.

items.title: 博通執行長示警：AI投資人像在賭場下注！資金短缺恐成產業最大瓶頸
items.title_en: Broadcom CEO Warns AI Investors Are Like Gamblers in a Casino! Funding Shortages May Become the Industry's Biggest Bottleneck
paras: 博通執行長陳福陽警告，許多追逐人工智慧(AI)熱潮的投資者，可能根本不了解自己投資的標的，最終反而像是走進賭場。他也質疑AI實驗室能否將龐大的算力需求轉化為可持續的營收與獲利，並指出，隨著AI產業持續擴張，資金不足可能取代晶片、記憶體與電力短缺，成為產業發展最大的瓶頸。
超大型雲端服務商持續投入數十億美元興建資料中心，為這波AI基礎建設熱潮提供強勁動能，而替科技巨頭設計客製化AI晶片的博通 (Broadcom) (AVGO-US)，則是主要受益者之一。根據公司財報，自2023年底以來，博通AI半導體業務累計營收約680億美元。在截至2026年8月2日的2026會計年度第三季，博通AI半導體營收更年增逾2倍，達167億美元，超過去年同期的3倍。
然而，博通業績大幅成長，並不代表整個AI產業鏈都能順利獲利。根據《彭博社》報導，博通執行長陳福陽上周在新加坡舉行的星展銀行亞洲未來前瞻大會上表示，許多投資者對自己的投資標的「根本一無所知」，卻抱持極高預期，最後可能發現自己「宛如置身於賭場之中」。
博通為頂尖AI實驗室提供建構運算系統所需的硬體，能直接從晶片銷售與相關產品需求中受惠。但對採購大量運算資源的AI實驗室而言，挑戰則在於必須找到足夠多願意付費的客戶，才能支應模型開發、訓練及日常運作的龐大成本。
陳福陽指出，OpenAI截至9月底的年化營收據報已達500億美元，顯示前沿AI模型確實存在龐大的商業化機會。不過，年化營收是根據當前營收速度推算出的全年水準，並不代表公司過去12個月實際取得相同金額的收入，更不能直接視為獲利。
陳福陽表示，OpenAI目前仍處於虧損狀態，原因在於公司持續將大量資金投入模型訓練。他認為，現階段的數據只能說明前沿生成式AI模型具有可觀的潛在營收成長空間，尚不足以證明相關企業已建立能夠長期獲利的商業模式。OpenAI預計今年僅模型訓練支出就將超過250億美元，顯示即使營收快速擴大，高昂的運算與研發成本仍可能侵蝕獲利。
AI產業另一項隱憂，是未來資本能否持續到位。隨著AI資料中心、晶片及運算基礎設施的投資規模不斷攀升，部分分析師預期，明年AI資本支出的成長速度可能放緩。陳福陽認為，相較於記憶體、半導體或電力供應不足，資金短缺「可能才是AI產業最大的制約因素」。
市場已開始出現投資人重新評估AI基礎建設融資需求的跡象。《彭博社》報導，由輝達 (NVIDIA) (NVDA-US) 支持的澳洲資料中心業者Firmus，原本計畫進行首次公開募股(IPO)，但由於投資者對預定發行價格的需求疲弱，公司已於10月9日撤回上市計畫。這項決定反映市場對AI基礎設施企業估值及融資條件的審慎態度，也凸顯即使產業前景受到看好，企業仍須取得足夠資金，才能支撐後續擴張。
不過，融資市場轉趨謹慎，並不代表AI運算需求已經降溫。英特爾 (Intel) (INTC-US) 執行長陳立武在同一場會議上表示，根據《彭博社》報導，硬體供應短缺的情況可能還會持續兩至三年。這意味著晶片及相關設備需求仍可能維持強勁，但需求旺盛與企業能否獲利，仍是兩個不同的問題。若AI業者無法將持續增加的基礎設施支出轉化為足夠的付費需求，即使市場需要更多晶片，也不代表相關投資一定合理。
除了AI模型開發商面臨獲利壓力，陳福陽也對企業客戶使用AI的方式提出批評。他指出，不少企業花錢購買詞元(token)進行各種AI實驗，卻沒有先確認哪些應用能真正改善營運效率或帶來財務回報，導致資金不斷消耗，卻未能創造相應價值。
他以童年在遊戲廳玩街機為例，形容部分企業的AI投資就像拿著父母給的10美元遊戲幣，在短短10分鐘內全部花光，最後卻什麼也沒得到。陳福陽認為，企業若只是為了跟上AI趨勢而不斷投入資金，卻沒有明確的應用目標與成效衡量方式，最終可能只是增加成本，而非提高生產力或獲利能力。
這項疑慮也與麥肯錫8月公布的AI投資回報調查相呼應。調查顯示，80%的受訪者認為AI提升了個人工作效率，但只有37%表示AI已對所在機構的息稅前利潤(EBIT)產生正面貢獻。此外，約五分之一的受訪者指出，包括詞元成本在內的AI相關營運支出，已限制所在機構進一步採用這項技術。

整體而言，AI產業正面臨需求成長與商業回報之間的落差。從博通AI半導體營收快速攀升，到AI實驗室持續承擔高額訓練成本，再到企業客戶尚未普遍將AI轉化為利潤，市場需要評估的已不只是晶片需求還能成長多久，也包括相關企業能否建立可持續的收入來源，以及投資者是否願意繼續為龐大的資本支出提供資金。對AI產業而言，真正的考驗不僅是能否打造更強大的模型與運算系統，更在於能否把技術需求轉化為長期、可衡量且足以支應成本的商業價值。
paras_en: Broadcom CEO Chen Fu-yang warned that many investors chasing the AI hype may not understand the assets they are investing in at all, ending up feeling like they have walked into a casino. He also questioned whether AI labs can turn massive compute demand into sustainable revenue and profit, noting that as the AI industry expands, a lack of funding could replace chip, memory and power shortages as the biggest bottleneck to growth.

Huge cloud providers continue to pour tens of billions of dollars into data centers, fueling the AI infrastructure boom, and Broadcom (AVGO-US), which designs custom AI chips for tech giants, is one of the main beneficiaries. According to its financials, Broadcom’s AI semiconductor business has generated about $68 billion in cumulative revenue since the end of 2023. In the third quarter of its fiscal 2026 year ending August 2, 2026, AI semiconductor revenue more than doubled year‑over‑year to $16.7 billion, more than three times the same period a year earlier.

However, Broadcom’s rapid growth does not mean the entire AI supply chain can profit smoothly. Bloomberg reported that Broadcom CEO Chen Fu-yang said at DBS Bank’s Asia Future Outlook conference in Singapore last week that many investors know “absolutely nothing” about what they are backing yet hold sky‑high expectations, and may end up feeling “as if they are in a casino.”

Broadcom supplies the hardware that top AI labs need to build compute systems, allowing it to benefit directly from chip sales and related product demand. But for AI labs that purchase massive compute resources, the challenge is finding enough paying customers to cover the huge costs of model development, training and day‑to‑day operations.

Chen pointed out that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was reported at $50 billion as of the end of September, showing that frontier AI models indeed have huge commercial potential. However, annualized revenue is a projection based on current revenue pace, not the actual amount earned over the past 12 months, and it cannot be taken as profit.

He added that OpenAI is still loss‑making because it continues to pour large sums into model training. He believes current data only show that cutting‑edge generative AI models have significant revenue growth potential, but that does not yet prove that the companies have built long‑term profitable business models. OpenAI expects model‑training expenses alone to exceed $25 billion this year, indicating that even rapid revenue expansion may be eroded by high compute and R&D costs.

Another hidden risk for the AI industry is whether capital will keep flowing. As investment in AI data centers, chips and compute infrastructure keeps climbing, some analysts expect AI capital‑expenditure growth to slow next year. Chen argues that, compared with shortages of memory, semiconductors or power, a funding shortfall “may be the biggest constraint on the AI industry.”

The market is already showing signs that investors are reassessing financing needs for AI infrastructure. Bloomberg reported that Firmus, an Australian data‑center operator backed by NVIDIA (NVDA‑US), had planned an IPO but withdrew the filing on October 9 after weak demand for the proposed price, reflecting a cautious stance on valuations and financing conditions for AI infrastructure firms and underscoring that even a rosy industry outlook requires sufficient capital for expansion.

Nevertheless, a more cautious financing environment does not mean AI compute demand has cooled. Intel (INTC‑US) CEO Pat Gelsinger said at the same conference that, according to Bloomberg, hardware supply shortages could persist for two to three more years. This suggests chip and related equipment demand may stay strong, but strong demand and corporate profitability are separate issues. If AI firms cannot turn rising infrastructure spend into enough paying demand, more chips in the market does not guarantee sensible investment.

Beyond pressure on AI model developers, Chen also criticized how corporate customers use AI. He noted many firms spend money buying tokens for various AI experiments without first confirming which applications truly improve operational efficiency or deliver financial returns, leading to continuous cash burn without corresponding value creation.

He likened it to his childhood experience of spending a $10 token bundle at an arcade, watching it disappear in ten minutes with nothing to show for it. Chen warned that if companies keep pouring money into AI just to keep up with the trend, without clear use‑case goals and performance metrics, they will merely add costs rather than boost productivity or profitability.

The concern echoes a McKinsey survey released in August on AI investment returns. The survey found 80% of respondents say AI has improved personal work efficiency, but only 37% say AI has positively contributed to their organization’s EBIT. About one‑fifth of respondents said AI‑related operating costs, including token expenses, are limiting further adoption.

Overall, the AI industry faces a gap between growing demand and commercial returns. From Broadcom’s soaring AI semiconductor revenue, to AI labs shouldering high training costs, to corporate customers still struggling to turn AI into profit, the market must assess not only how long chip demand can grow but also whether companies can build sustainable revenue streams and whether investors will keep funding massive capital outlays. For AI, the real test is not just building bigger models and compute systems, but converting technological demand into long‑term, measurable, cost‑covering business value.

items.title: 響應馬斯克？《巴隆》點名巴菲特：應考慮贈波克夏股票給全美兒童
items.title_en: Responding to Musk? Barron's Calls on Buffett to Consider Giving Berkshire Shares to All U.S. Children
paras: 隨著特斯拉 (Tesla) 暨 SpaceX 執行長馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 拋出震撼彈，宣布將把其持有的 SpaceX 股份贈予全美每位兒童，引發各界熱議。外媒《巴隆週刊》(Barron's) 分析指出，包括「股神」華倫·巴菲特 (Warren Buffett) 在內的眾多千億級超級富豪，或許該考慮跟進這項創舉，藉此解決巨額財產善款撥付的難題，同時為美國下一代扎根投資與金融教育。
馬斯克日前於社群平台表示，將把旗下 SpaceX 約 1% 的股份 (估值約 100 億美元) 撥出，分送給全美近 7,000 萬名 18 歲以下的兒童，相當於每位兒童可獲得價值約 148 美元的股票。
巨額遺產捐贈時限逼近 巴菲特家族面臨考驗
現年 96 歲的波克夏·海瑟威 (Berkshire Hathaway) 前董事長巴菲特，目前持有價值約 1,500 億美元的波克夏股票。巴菲特先前曾規劃，要求其三名子女 (蘇珊、豪爾德與彼得) 在其身故後的 2034 年前將這筆鉅款全數捐出，且不打算建立如福特基金會般長期營運的基金會結構。
然而，巴菲特的三名子女坦言這項任務極具挑戰。
目前三人的基金會每年各自捐贈約 5 億美元，但若要在指定期限內消化巴菲特的遺產，未來每年需發放的善款將高達 150 億美元以上。
《巴隆週刊》分析建議，若巴菲特比照馬斯克模式，向全美每位兒童贈送一股波克夏 B 股 (BRK.B)，每位兒童將可獲得約 532 美元的資產。
這項行動預計耗資約 370 億美元，僅占巴菲特總財產的四分之一，但能極大化減輕其子女後續撥付善款的負擔。目前巴菲特對此提議尚未做出正面回應。
跨世代投資教育 啟動資本複利效應
這項建議若能實現，除了減輕基金會的運作負擔外，更被視為對美國下一代的長遠投資。
憑藉波克夏穩健的資產負債表與獲利能力，市場預期其股票在未來十年每年複合成長率可達近 10%。直接贈股不僅能提供實質財富，更能啟發年輕一代學習價值投資、金融知識以及傳承巴菲特的投資哲學。
除了巴菲特外，報導也點名了亞馬遜創辦人貝佐斯 (Jeff Bezos)、Meta 執行長祖克柏 (Mark Zuckerberg)、輝達執行長黃仁勳 (Jensen Huang) 以及 Google 共同創辦人佩吉 (Larry Page) 與布林 (Sergey Brin) 等身價突破千億美元的科技巨擘，認為這些企業領袖皆可借鏡馬斯克的創新慈善模式，為社會帶來更廣泛且深遠的正面影響。
paras_en: As Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk dropped a bombshell announcing he will donate his SpaceX shares to every child in the United States, the move sparked heated debate. Barron’s analysis notes that many trillion‑dollar‑worth super‑rich individuals, including the “Oracle of Omaha” Warren Buffett, might consider following suit to solve the challenge of allocating massive charitable wealth while rooting investment and financial education in the next generation of Americans.

Musk recently posted on social media that he will allocate roughly 1% of SpaceX – valued at about $10 billion – to the nearly 70 million children under 18 across the country, which works out to about $148 worth of stock per child.
The deadline for a massive estate donation is looming, and the Buffett family faces a test.

Now 96‑year‑old former Berkshire Hathaway chairman Warren Buffett holds roughly $150 billion of Berkshire stock. He has previously stipulated that his three children – Susan, Howard and Peter – must donate the entire amount by 2034, the year after his death, and he does not intend to set up a permanent foundation like the Ford Foundation.
However, Buffett’s three heirs admit that the task is extremely challenging.

Their respective family foundations currently give about $500 million each year, but to exhaust Buffett’s fortune within the prescribed timeframe, future annual charitable disbursements would need to exceed $15 billion.
Barron’s analysis suggests that, if Buffett mirrored Musk’s model and gave every U.S. child one share of Berkshire’s Class B stock (BRK.B), each child would receive roughly $532 in assets.

The proposal would cost about $37 billion – roughly a quarter of Buffett’s total wealth – but could dramatically reduce the burden on his heirs to fund future philanthropy. Buffett has not yet responded positively to the idea.
A cross‑generational investment education could unleash the power of compound capital.
If implemented, the plan would not only ease the operational load on the foundations but also be viewed as a long‑term investment in America’s next generation.

Leveraging Berkshire’s solid balance sheet and earnings power, the market expects its stock to compound at close to 10% annually over the next decade. Direct stock gifts would provide tangible wealth and inspire young people to learn value investing, financial literacy, and Buffett’s investment philosophy.

Beyond Buffett, the report also names other tech titans with net worths exceeding $100 billion – Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Google co‑founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin – as leaders who could emulate Musk’s innovative charitable model to generate broader, deeper social impact.

items.title_en: Is the AI Trading Honeymoon Over? Nvidia and Micron Lead the Recovery as This Week’s Heavyweight Earnings Test Confidence
paras: 經歷近兩周沉重賣壓後，投資人重新評估人工智慧(AI)支出的成長能否持續，包括美光(MU-US)、輝達(NVDA-US)在內的晶片股周一(19日)反彈。隨著第3季財報季展開，股市能否有更大幅度的回升，，將取決於本周大型科技企業財報能否消除市場對AI交易可持續性的疑慮，包括Meta Platforms(META-US)、特斯拉(TSLA-US)和SpaceX(SPCX-US)。
儘管大盤周一反彈，但更大幅度的回升，將取決於本周大型科技企業財報能否消除市場對AI交易可持續性的疑慮。Meta Platforms(META-US)與特斯拉(TSLA-US)等大型企業將公布財報，SpaceX(SPCX-US)則將於周二收盤後公布業績。

晶片股止跌回穩，財報季成多空分水嶺

輝達周一收漲1.4%，競爭對手超微(AMD-US)上漲約1.8%。今年以來受惠於AI需求的美光與英特爾(INTC-US)，股價分別上漲約3%與2.4%。SanDisk(SNDK-US)也反彈5.5%，iShares半導體ETF(SOXX-US)上漲1.7%。
提供AI運算雲端服務的新雲端業者Nebius Group(NBIS-US)股價也反彈2.9%。
晶片類股到上周五已連續八個交易日走跌，反映投資人質疑AI支出成長能否持續，並對OpenAI與Anthropic等未上市AI公司的財務進展報告提出疑問。
整體經濟情勢也加深市場疑慮。美國9月通膨升幅高於預期，可能促使聯準會(Fed)更積極升息，當利率走高，CoreWeave(CRWV-US)等大量借款、用於興建資料中心的公司將面臨壓力。
Zacks投資管理公司首席市場策略師Brian Mulberry表示，晶片股周一反彈，反映市場對AI支出及企業將AI產品變現的能力恢復信心。
隨著第3季財報季展開，Mulberry指出，投資人也將觀察其他產業的表現，以確認需求是否仍然強勁，而AI技術的採用程度是否還在持續提高。而晶片股周一的漲勢將有助於「扭轉過去幾個月的市場氣氛，重新建立正向動能」，尤其是在半導體領域。
截至目前，已公布第3季財報的47家標普500指數成分企業中，有85%獲利優於市場預期。整體標普500指數目前有望繳出29%的綜合獲利成長率。然而，多數科技業財報尚未公布，市場對這些企業的期待也相當高。
本周公布財報的大型企業包括Meta Platforms與特斯拉，SpaceX也將於周二盤後公布業績。

AI蜜月期已過，投資人改審視實質獲利

富國銀行投資研究所(Wells Fargo Investment Institute)的Sameer Samana表示，目前AI交易的走勢看來更像是一次「現實檢驗」，而非「全面崩解」。不過，他仍認為，未來幾天甚至幾周，市場可能持續壟罩在賣壓中。
Equity Armor Investments執行長Luke Rahbari認為，這波賣壓顯示，「AI交易的蜜月期可能已經結束」，投資人開始提出質疑，不再盲目接受高估值。
Rahbari指出，投資人接下來將尋找市場地位與創新能力最強的企業。隨著估值下修，輝達與超微等AI投資論述更具說服力的股票，也將提供更多重新進場的機會。他特別提到超微近期收購World Labs，認為這項交易將使超微「在掌握AI未來發展樣貌方面取得優勢」。
展望未來，Rahbari表示，投資人仍將對AI市場累積的債務規模感到不安。

資料中心擴張放緩，現有容量業者擁優勢

研究機構Radio Free Mobile創辦人Richard Windsor表示，在市場情緒更加不安的背景下，輝達本周在柏林舉行的GTC大會，以及Meta Platforms(META-US)即將公布的第3季財報，將是「恢復市場信心的關鍵，讓投資人相信AI基礎建設的擴張能夠兌現承諾」。
Windsor也指出，AI資料中心建置進度延誤的情況正日益增加。美國民眾反對在社區內興建資料中心，業者也面臨許可審批與電力短缺等問題。
《華爾街日報》(WSJ)報導，微軟(MSFT-US)周一據傳決定不再與英國新雲端業者Nscale Global Holdings(NSCL-US)旗下資料中心洽談算力採購協議，原因是電力供應面臨挑戰。
儘管市場對新資料中心的疑慮升高，Windsor在致客戶的報告中指出，已經營運資料中心的企業仍有「一線曙光」。目前資料中心營運商對外提供運算容量的收費，處於「超常水準」，五年期的年化報酬率可達45%至85%。
Windsor指出，隨著更多算力陸續上線，這種成長最終將回歸常態，但考量建置延誤，這個過程「看來將比預期花更長時間」，因此，現在就有可供出售容量的業者將獲得顯著優勢。
他認為，雲端服務供應商將因此受惠，而xAI與Meta可能是主要受益者，因為他認為這兩家公司擁有最多可額外出售給客戶的運算容量。
整體而言，Windsor表示，AI交易背後的基本驅動因素「幾乎沒有改變」，因為過去一個月公布財報的企業，其運算容量至少都已被預訂至未來12個月。這為明年的市場表現奠定良好基礎，但預期資料中心的短期定價將開始回歸正常水準。
paras_en: After nearly two weeks of heavy selling pressure, investors are re‑evaluating whether growth in AI spending can be sustained, and chip stocks including Micron (MU‑US) and Nvidia (NVDA‑US) rebounded on Monday (the 19th). As the Q3 earnings season gets underway, the market’s ability to rally more sharply will hinge on whether this week’s big‑tech earnings can allay doubts about the sustainability of AI‑driven trading, including those from Meta Platforms (META‑US), Tesla (TSLA‑US) and SpaceX (SPCX‑US).

Even though the broader market bounced back on Monday, a larger rebound will depend on whether this week’s major tech earnings can dispel concerns about the durability of AI‑driven trading. Large companies such as Meta Platforms (META‑US) and Tesla (TSLA‑US) will release earnings, while SpaceX (SPCX‑US) will report results after the close on Tuesday.

Chip stocks halted their decline and steadied, making earnings season a watershed for bulls and bears. Nvidia rose 1.4% on Monday, while rival AMD (AMD‑US) gained about 1.8%. Micron and Intel (INTC‑US), both beneficiaries of AI demand this year, climbed roughly 3% and 2.4% respectively. SanDisk (SNDK‑US) also jumped 5.5%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX‑US) was up 1.7%.
Nebius Group (NBIS‑US), a cloud provider that offers AI compute services, saw its stock rebound 2.9%.

Chip stocks had logged eight consecutive trading days of declines through last Friday, reflecting investor doubts about whether AI‑related spending can keep growing and raising questions about the financial progress of private AI firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Overall economic conditions have deepened market concerns. U.S. September inflation rose more than expected, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to accelerate rate hikes. Higher rates would pressure heavily leveraged, data‑center‑building companies like CoreWeave (CRWV‑US).

Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, said the Monday bounce in chip stocks reflects a restored confidence in AI spending and companies’ ability to monetize AI products.

As the Q3 earnings season unfolds, Mulberry noted investors will also watch other sectors to confirm whether demand remains robust and whether AI adoption continues to rise. The chip‑stock rally on Monday should help "reverse the market mood of the past few months and re‑establish positive momentum," especially in semiconductors.

To date, among the 47 S&P 500 constituents that have reported Q3 results, 85% have posted earnings above market expectations. The S&P 500 overall is on track for a 29% combined earnings growth rate. However, most tech earnings are still pending, and market expectations for those companies remain high.
Large companies reporting earnings this week include Meta Platforms and Tesla, with SpaceX also set to release results after the market closes on Tuesday.

The AI honeymoon appears to be over, and investors are re‑examining real profitability. Sameer Samana of Wells Fargo Investment Institute said the current AI‑trading trend looks more like a "reality check" than a "total collapse," but he still expects the market could remain under selling pressure for days or even weeks ahead.

Luke Rahbari, CEO of Equity Armor Investments, said the recent sell‑off suggests "the AI trading honeymoon may have ended," as investors begin to question lofty valuations rather than accept them blindly.

Rahbari added that investors will now look for companies with the strongest market positions and innovation capabilities. With valuations trimmed, stocks like Nvidia and AMD, whose AI investment theses are now more compelling, will offer more re‑entry opportunities. He specifically cited AMD’s recent acquisition of World Labs, believing the deal gives AMD an edge in shaping AI’s future development.
Looking ahead, Rahbari said investors will remain uneasy about the scale of debt accumulated in the AI market.

Data‑center expansion is slowing, giving existing capacity providers an advantage. Richard Windsor, founder of research firm Radio Free Mobile, said that amid heightened market anxiety, Nvidia’s GTC conference in Berlin this week and Meta Platforms’ upcoming Q3 earnings will be "key to restoring market confidence and convincing investors that AI infrastructure expansion can deliver on its promises."

Windsor also noted that delays in building AI data centers are becoming increasingly common. Public opposition to data‑center construction in U.S. communities, along with permitting hurdles and power shortages, are adding to the challenges.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Microsoft (MSFT‑US) allegedly decided on Monday not to pursue a compute‑capacity purchase agreement with the UK‑based new cloud provider Nscale Global Holdings (NSCL‑US) due to power‑supply concerns.

Despite rising doubts about new data centers, Windsor said in a client briefing that operators already running facilities still see "a glimmer of hope." Current pricing for external compute capacity remains "exceptionally high," with five‑year annualized returns ranging from 45% to 85%.

Windsor pointed out that as more compute capacity comes online, growth will eventually normalize, but given construction delays, this process "looks set to take longer than expected," giving a competitive edge to providers that already have sellable capacity today.
He believes cloud service providers will benefit, with xAI and Meta likely being the primary beneficiaries, as they have the most excess compute capacity to sell to customers.

Overall, Windsor concluded that the fundamental drivers behind AI trading have "hardly changed," since companies that reported earnings over the past month have already booked compute capacity out to the next 12 months. This lays a solid foundation for next year’s market performance, though short‑term data‑center pricing is expected to revert to more normal levels.

paras: 2026年10月20日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 美股19日收盤漲跌互見，半導體與AI概念股跌深反彈，帶動那斯達克指數上漲1.11%，費城半導體指數也終止連八跌。不過，標普500多數類股收黑，顯示買盤集中大型權值股，市場對高利率與AI建設融資的疑慮仍未消退。
道瓊指數下跌36.38點、跌幅0.07%，收51,966.03點；標普500指數上漲31.29點、漲幅0.41%，收7,690.73點；那斯達克指數上漲290.85點，收26,430.89點。費半指數上漲1.6%，結束2008年10月以來最長連跌紀錄，先前八個交易日累計重挫約15.7%。
亞馬遜獲摩根士丹利列為首選股，股價大漲5%；特斯拉上漲3.8%，帶動非必需消費類股勁揚2.7%。英特爾獲摩根大通調升評等至「中立」，收漲2.4%。
AI雲端業者CoreWeave則由漲轉跌0.4%。公司雖獲高盛升評至「買進」，500億美元債務負擔仍牽動市場信心，上週股價已重挫逾25%。同業Nebius與Iren分別上漲2.9%、2.7%。
反彈力道尚未全面擴散。標普500的11大類股中，七類收黑，公用事業與房地產分別下跌2%、1.2%；紐約證交所及那斯達克市場均以下跌家數居多。美股成交量152.7億股，也低於近20個交易日均量172.6億股。
Rosenblatt Securities交易主管James指出，這波回升主要來自市場過度悲觀後的超賣反彈，基本面並未明顯變化。隨著SpaceX週二、Meta與特斯拉週三公布財報，科技股能否延續漲勢仍待檢驗。此外，中東攻擊事件推升美國原油期貨上漲2.2%，收每桶103.66美元，也削弱油價先前回落對股市的支撐。

paras_en: On October 20, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – US equities closed mixed on the 19th, with semiconductor and AI‑related stocks falling sharply then rebounding, lifting the Nasdaq index 1.11% and ending an eight‑day slide in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. However, most S&P 500 sectors were down, showing buying concentrated in large‑cap stocks and lingering concerns over high interest rates and AI‑related financing.

The Dow Jones fell 36.38 points, or 0.07%, to 51,966.03; the S&P 500 rose 31.29 points, or 0.41%, to 7,690.73; the Nasdaq gained 290.85 points to close at 26,430.89. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 1.6%, snapping its longest losing streak since October 2008 after an eight‑day slide that had erased about 15.7% cumulatively.

Amazon was named a top pick by Morgan Stanley, surging 5%; Tesla rose 3.8%, helping non‑essential consumer stocks climb 2.7%. Intel was upgraded by JPMorgan to a “Neutral” rating and finished up 2.4%.

AI‑cloud provider CoreWeave flipped to a 0.4% decline after previously rising. Although Goldman Sachs upgraded the company to “Buy,” its $50 billion debt load continues to weigh on confidence, and the stock had already tumbled more than 25% last week. Peers Nebius and Iren rose 2.9% and 2.7% respectively.

The rebound has not yet spread broadly. Of the S&P 500’s 11 sector groups, seven closed lower, with utilities and real estate down 2% and 1.2% respectively; the NYSE and Nasdaq both saw more decliners than advancers. US equity volume was 15.27 billion shares, below the 20‑day average of 17.26 billion shares.

James, head of trading at Rosenblatt Securities, said the bounce is mainly a short‑covering rally after an overly pessimistic market, with fundamentals unchanged. With SpaceX reporting on Tuesday and Meta and Tesla on Wednesday, it remains to be seen whether tech stocks can sustain the gains. Meanwhile, Middle‑East attacks pushed US crude futures up 2.2% to $103.66 a barrel, weakening the earlier oil‑price support for equities.

items.title: 黃仁勳週三登場！輝達GTC五大看點曝光 能否成AI股反攻關鍵？
items.title_en: Jensen Huang Takes the Stage on Wednesday! Nvidia GTC's Five Key Themes Unveiled – A Crucial Test for AI Stock Rally
paras: AI產業上週接連遭遇市場考驗，AI投資邏輯正面臨一輪罕見的壓力測試。在此背景下，輝達(Nvidia)(NVDA-US)即將舉行的GTC大會，或將為觀察下一階段AI產業的發展方向提供重要線索。
NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026將於當地時間10月20日至22日在德國柏林舉行。輝達CEO黃仁勳將於台灣時間10月21日17:00至19:00發表主題演講，分享對AI技術與產業發展的最新展望。與其單純關注是否推出新產品，市場更值得留意的是：當AI投資進入回報驗證階段，輝達將如何進一步拓展AI基建需求、推動AI代理實施，以及將AI能力延伸至工業與物理世界。
AI投資進入驗證期，GTC為何備受關注？
過去幾年，AI產業的投資主線相對清晰：大模型能力持續提升，推動算力需求增長，進而帶動GPU、伺服器、網絡設備及資料中心等環節的資本開支。
但隨著AI基建投入不斷擴大，市場關注點正在發生變化。
首先，算力需求增長，不等於所有算力投資都能獲得理想回報。 資料中心建設涉及晶片採購、電力供應、網絡設備及融資成本，只有當企業能夠持續獲得客戶需求、提高算力利用率並實現商業化，巨額投入才有望形成可持續的收益。
其次，AI應用正從模型訓練走向推理與實際部署。企業不再只關注模型能力，也開始重視推理成本、運行效率、數據安全，以及AI能否真正融入業務流程。
因此，本次GTC的重要觀察重點，是輝達如何完善從晶片、系統、軟體到應用的AI生態，以及這些技術進展能否創造新的需求。
五大主題浮現，AI產業下一站看哪裡？
從本次GTC Berlin公布的議程來看，大會不僅聚焦算力基建，還將涉及主權AI與企業AI、AI原生企業、AI安全、AI工廠，以及物理AI等方向。
1. 主權AI與企業AI：AI基建需求能否進一步擴大？
在主權AI與企業AI環節，討論重點是各國及企業如何利用自身數據、行業知識與基礎設施，建設並部署自己的AI能力。嘉賓包括達梭系統CEO Pascal Daloz、德國電信CEO Tim Höttges，以及Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch。
AI需求不再只來自少數大型模型公司。政府、電信運營商、工業企業及其他大型機構，也可能因數據主權、合規要求及業務效率而建設專屬AI系統。
若企業級AI部署持續擴大，算力基建、私有化部署、企業級軟體及數據安全等領域，都有望獲得新的需求。
2. AI原生企業：AI能否從技術突破走向商業增長？
AI原生企業環節將探討歐洲創業者與投資者如何利用AI技術，打造新一代企業。相關嘉賓包括Corti.AI聯合創辦人Andreas Cleve、General Catalyst的Jeannette zu Fürstenberg、Black Forest Labs共同創辦人Robin Rombach，以及Ineffable Intelligence創辦人David Silver。
這項環節的重點在於AI應用的商業化進展。 如果AI不再只是提升既有軟體的效率，而是能夠催生新的產品、服務及商業模式，AI產業的增長來源便有望從基礎設施投資，進一步延伸至應用與服務收入。
不過，客戶付費意願、收入增長及盈利能力，仍是驗證商業模式能否成立的關鍵。
3. AI安全與企業級部署：代理實施還缺什麼？
隨著AI Agent逐步具備調用工具、存取數據及執行任務的能力，安全問題也變得更加重要。本次相關環節邀請CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz、Hugging Face創辦人Thomas Wolf，以及Red Hat的Chris Wright參與討論。
當AI從回答問題轉向執行任務，企業必須確保AI能夠在授權範圍內存取數據、執行操作，並具備可靠的安全防護機制。
因此，AI代理的普及不僅涉及模型能力，也涉及身份驗證、權限管理、網絡安全及企業軟體架構。AI安全與企業級軟體能否創造更多商業價值，將取決於實際部署規模與客戶需求。
4. AI工廠：算力基建的競爭將走向系統效率
AI工廠是本次GTC的另一項重要議題，相關討論將聚焦如何透過基礎設施建設，提高生產效率並帶動經濟增長。代表嘉賓包括施耐德電氣的Frédéric Godemel、Brookfield 的Siko Rashid，以及NEBIUS 創辦人兼CEO Arkady Volozh。
AI工廠並不只是採購GPU，而是涵蓋運算、網絡、記憶體、供電、散熱及軟體調度的完整系統。
當AI集群規模持續擴大，單一晶片的性能已不足以決定整體效率。如何提高集群利用率、降低每單位運算成本，以及縮短資料中心部署週期，都將影響算力投資的回報。
因此，除了GPU需求，高速互連、網絡設備、電力及資料中心基建等環節也值得關注。
5. 物理AI與工業AI：AI將走出資料中心
Physical AI，即物理AI，將AI能力延伸至機器人、汽車及工業設備等真實世界場景。本次相關環節的嘉賓包括Agile Robots的陳兆鵬（Zhaopeng Chen）、西門子醫療的Arthur Kaindl、賓士 CEO Ola Källenius，以及Humanoid的Artem Sokolov。
與主要處理文字、圖像及數據的生成式AI不同，Physical AI需要理解物理環境，並透過感知、推理、模擬及控制，完成現實世界中的任務。
這一方向有望將AI需求延伸至機器人、工業自動化、智慧汽車及相關運算平台。
不過，從技術展示走向規模化商業部署仍有距離。機器人的實際作業能力、成本、可靠性及客戶採用速度，才是判斷產業能否持續增長的關鍵。
投資觀察重點
綜合本次大會議程，市場可以重點觀察以下三個方向：
第一，算力需求能否持續擴張。 除了輝達的晶片與系統布局，企業級AI、主權AI及AI工廠是否帶來新的基建需求，也將影響產業鏈的成長空間。
第二，AI代理能否創造實際商業價值。 若AI逐步從輔助工具走向自主執行任務，推理運算、安全軟體及企業級部署可能獲得更多機會，但仍需驗證成本與收入之間的關係。
第三，物理AI能否開啟新的增長空間。 機器人、工業自動化及智慧汽車等場景，可能拓寬AI的應用邊界，但商業化速度與盈利模式仍有待觀察。
需要注意的是，GTC是技術與產業交流的重要窗口，並不意味著大會上的每一項技術進展都會立即轉化為企業收入或股價催化。
在AI投資邏輯面臨重新評估之際，真正決定產業長期走勢的，仍是算力需求能否持續、資本開支能否獲得回報，以及AI應用能否形成可持續的商業模式。
paras_en: AI industry faced market tests last week, putting AI investment logic under rare pressure. Against this backdrop, Nvidia's (NVDA-US) upcoming GTC conference could provide key clues about the next phase of AI development.

NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 will be held in Berlin, Germany from October 20‑22 local time. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will deliver a keynote from 17:00‑19:00 Taiwan time on October 21, sharing the latest outlook on AI technology and industry development. Beyond new product launches, the market should watch how Nvidia expands AI infrastructure demand, drives AI agent deployment, and extends AI capabilities to industrial and physical worlds as AI investment moves into a return‑validation stage.
Why is GTC drawing attention as AI investment enters the validation phase?

In recent years the main investment theme in AI has been clear: larger model capabilities drive higher compute demand, which in turn fuels capital spending on GPUs, servers, networking gear and data‑center infrastructure.
But as AI infrastructure spending keeps expanding, market focus is shifting.

First, growing compute demand does not guarantee that every compute investment will yield ideal returns. Data‑center builds involve chip purchases, power supply, networking equipment and financing costs; only when companies can sustain customer demand, improve compute utilization and commercialize the technology will massive outlays translate into sustainable earnings.

Second, AI applications are moving from model training to inference and real‑world deployment. Enterprises are no longer only concerned with model capability; they also care about inference cost, operational efficiency, data security, and whether AI can truly integrate into business processes.
Thus the key observation at this GTC is how Nvidia will refine the AI ecosystem—from chips and systems to software and applications—and whether these advances can generate new demand.
Five major themes emerge – where is the AI industry headed next?

The Berlin GTC agenda shows the conference will not only focus on compute infrastructure but also cover sovereign AI and enterprise AI, AI‑native enterprises, AI safety, AI factories, and physical AI.
1. Sovereign AI and Enterprise AI: Can AI infrastructure demand expand further?

In the sovereign and enterprise AI track, the discussion centers on how nations and companies can use their own data, industry knowledge and infrastructure to build and deploy their own AI capabilities. Guests include Dassault Systèmes CEO Pascal Daloz, Deutsche Telekom CEO Tim Höttges, and Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch.

AI demand is no longer limited to a few large‑model firms. Governments, telecom operators, industrial firms and other large institutions may also build dedicated AI systems for data‑sovereignty, compliance and efficiency reasons.
If enterprise‑level AI deployments keep growing, compute infrastructure, private‑cloud deployments, enterprise software and data‑security segments are likely to see fresh demand.
2. AI‑Native Enterprises: Can AI move from technical breakthroughs to commercial growth?

The AI‑native enterprise session will explore how European founders and investors are leveraging AI to create the next generation of companies. Speakers include Corti.AI co‑founder Andreas Cleve, General Catalyst’s Jeannette zu Fürstenberg, Black Forest Labs co‑founder Robin Rombach, and Ineffable Intelligence founder David Silver.

The focus here is the commercialization of AI applications. If AI can do more than boost existing software efficiency—by spawning new products, services and business models—growth can shift from pure infrastructure spending to revenue from applications and services.
Nevertheless, customer willingness to pay, revenue growth and profitability remain the litmus tests for any business model.
3. AI Safety and Enterprise‑Scale Deployment: What’s still missing for agent implementation?

As AI agents gain the ability to call tools, access data and execute tasks, security concerns become paramount. This segment features CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz, Hugging Face founder Thomas Wolf, and Red Hat’s Chris Wright.
When AI moves from answering questions to performing tasks, enterprises must ensure agents can access data and act only within authorized bounds, backed by robust security safeguards.

Thus the spread of AI agents involves not just model capability but also authentication, permission management, cyber‑security and enterprise software architecture. Whether AI safety and enterprise software can create added commercial value will depend on deployment scale and customer needs.
4. AI Factories: Compute infrastructure competition will shift toward system efficiency

AI factories are another key GTC topic, focusing on how infrastructure builds can boost production efficiency and drive economic growth. Speakers include Schneider Electric’s Frédéric Godemel, Brookfield’s Siko Rashid, and NEBIUS founder‑CEO Arkady Volozh.
An AI factory is more than buying GPUs; it encompasses compute, networking, memory, power, cooling and software scheduling as an integrated system.

As AI cluster sizes keep growing, the performance of a single chip no longer determines overall efficiency. Improving cluster utilization, lowering per‑unit compute cost and shortening data‑center deployment cycles will all affect compute investment returns.
Therefore, beyond GPU demand, high‑speed interconnects, networking gear, power and data‑center construction merit close attention.
5. Physical AI and Industrial AI: AI Leaving the Data Center

Physical AI extends AI capabilities to robots, cars and industrial equipment in real‑world settings. Speakers include Agile Robots’ Zhaopeng Chen, Siemens Healthineers’ Arthur Kaindl, Mercedes‑Benz CEO Ola Källenius, and Humanoid’s Artem Sokolov.

Unlike generative AI that mainly handles text, images and data, Physical AI must understand the physical environment and use perception, reasoning, simulation and control to accomplish real‑world tasks.
This direction could push AI demand into robotics, industrial automation, smart vehicles and related compute platforms.

However, moving from tech demos to scaled commercial deployment still has a way to go. The actual operational capability, cost, reliability and adoption speed of robots will determine whether the sector can sustain growth.
Investment Observation Points
Based on the conference agenda, the market can focus on three key areas:

First, whether compute demand can keep expanding. In addition to Nvidia’s chip and system roadmap, enterprise AI, sovereign AI and AI factories could generate new infrastructure demand, influencing the industry‑chain growth horizon.

Second, whether AI agents can create real commercial value. If agents evolve from assistance tools to autonomous task executors, inference compute, security software and enterprise‑scale deployments may see more opportunities, though the cost‑revenue relationship still needs validation.

Third, whether physical AI can open new growth space. Robotics, industrial automation and smart‑vehicle scenarios could broaden AI’s application frontier, but commercialization speed and viable profit models remain to be seen.

It’s worth noting that GTC is an important venue for technology and industry exchange, but not every technical advance presented will instantly translate into corporate revenue or stock‑price catalysts.

As AI investment logic is re‑evaluated, the long‑term trajectory of the industry will still hinge on whether compute demand remains sustainable, capital spending yields returns, and AI applications can form enduring business models.

items.title: 博通執行長示警：AI投資人像在賭場下注！資金短缺恐成產業最大瓶頸
items.title_en: Broadcom CEO Warns AI Investors Are Like Gamblers in a Casino! Funding Shortages May Become the Industry's Biggest Bottleneck
paras: 博通執行長陳福陽警告，許多追逐人工智慧(AI)熱潮的投資者，可能根本不了解自己投資的標的，最終反而像是走進賭場。他也質疑AI實驗室能否將龐大的算力需求轉化為可持續的營收與獲利，並指出，隨著AI產業持續擴張，資金不足可能取代晶片、記憶體與電力短缺，成為產業發展最大的瓶頸。
超大型雲端服務商持續投入數十億美元興建資料中心，為這波AI基礎建設熱潮提供強勁動能，而替科技巨頭設計客製化AI晶片的博通 (Broadcom) (AVGO-US)，則是主要受益者之一。根據公司財報，自2023年底以來，博通AI半導體業務累計營收約680億美元。在截至2026年8月2日的2026會計年度第三季，博通AI半導體營收更年增逾2倍，達167億美元，超過去年同期的3倍。
然而，博通業績大幅成長，並不代表整個AI產業鏈都能順利獲利。根據《彭博社》報導，博通執行長陳福陽上周在新加坡舉行的星展銀行亞洲未來前瞻大會上表示，許多投資者對自己的投資標的「根本一無所知」，卻抱持極高預期，最後可能發現自己「宛如置身於賭場之中」。
博通為頂尖AI實驗室提供建構運算系統所需的硬體，能直接從晶片銷售與相關產品需求中受惠。但對採購大量運算資源的AI實驗室而言，挑戰則在於必須找到足夠多願意付費的客戶，才能支應模型開發、訓練及日常運作的龐大成本。
陳福陽指出，OpenAI截至9月底的年化營收據報已達500億美元，顯示前沿AI模型確實存在龐大的商業化機會。不過，年化營收是根據當前營收速度推算出的全年水準，並不代表公司過去12個月實際取得相同金額的收入，更不能直接視為獲利。
陳福陽表示，OpenAI目前仍處於虧損狀態，原因在於公司持續將大量資金投入模型訓練。他認為，現階段的數據只能說明前沿生成式AI模型具有可觀的潛在營收成長空間，尚不足以證明相關企業已建立能夠長期獲利的商業模式。OpenAI預計今年僅模型訓練支出就將超過250億美元，顯示即使營收快速擴大，高昂的運算與研發成本仍可能侵蝕獲利。
AI產業另一項隱憂，是未來資本能否持續到位。隨著AI資料中心、晶片及運算基礎設施的投資規模不斷攀升，部分分析師預期，明年AI資本支出的成長速度可能放緩。陳福陽認為，相較於記憶體、半導體或電力供應不足，資金短缺「可能才是AI產業最大的制約因素」。
市場已開始出現投資人重新評估AI基礎建設融資需求的跡象。《彭博社》報導，由輝達 (NVIDIA) (NVDA-US) 支持的澳洲資料中心業者Firmus，原本計畫進行首次公開募股(IPO)，但由於投資者對預定發行價格的需求疲弱，公司已於10月9日撤回上市計畫。這項決定反映市場對AI基礎設施企業估值及融資條件的審慎態度，也凸顯即使產業前景受到看好，企業仍須取得足夠資金，才能支撐後續擴張。
不過，融資市場轉趨謹慎，並不代表AI運算需求已經降溫。英特爾 (Intel) (INTC-US) 執行長陳立武在同一場會議上表示，根據《彭博社》報導，硬體供應短缺的情況可能還會持續兩至三年。這意味著晶片及相關設備需求仍可能維持強勁，但需求旺盛與企業能否獲利，仍是兩個不同的問題。若AI業者無法將持續增加的基礎設施支出轉化為足夠的付費需求，即使市場需要更多晶片，也不代表相關投資一定合理。
除了AI模型開發商面臨獲利壓力，陳福陽也對企業客戶使用AI的方式提出批評。他指出，不少企業花錢購買詞元(token)進行各種AI實驗，卻沒有先確認哪些應用能真正改善營運效率或帶來財務回報，導致資金不斷消耗，卻未能創造相應價值。
他以童年在遊戲廳玩街機為例，形容部分企業的AI投資就像拿著父母給的10美元遊戲幣，在短短10分鐘內全部花光，最後卻什麼也沒得到。陳福陽認為，企業若只是為了跟上AI趨勢而不斷投入資金，卻沒有明確的應用目標與成效衡量方式，最終可能只是增加成本，而非提高生產力或獲利能力。
這項疑慮也與麥肯錫8月公布的AI投資回報調查相呼應。調查顯示，80%的受訪者認為AI提升了個人工作效率，但只有37%表示AI已對所在機構的息稅前利潤(EBIT)產生正面貢獻。此外，約五分之一的受訪者指出，包括詞元成本在內的AI相關營運支出，已限制所在機構進一步採用這項技術。

整體而言，AI產業正面臨需求成長與商業回報之間的落差。從博通AI半導體營收快速攀升，到AI實驗室持續承擔高額訓練成本，再到企業客戶尚未普遍將AI轉化為利潤，市場需要評估的已不只是晶片需求還能成長多久，也包括相關企業能否建立可持續的收入來源，以及投資者是否願意繼續為龐大的資本支出提供資金。對AI產業而言，真正的考驗不僅是能否打造更強大的模型與運算系統，更在於能否把技術需求轉化為長期、可衡量且足以支應成本的商業價值。
paras_en: Broadcom CEO Chen Fu-yang warned that many investors chasing the AI hype may not understand the assets they are investing in at all, ending up feeling like they have walked into a casino. He also questioned whether AI labs can turn massive compute demand into sustainable revenue and profit, noting that as the AI industry expands, a lack of funding could replace chip, memory and power shortages as the biggest bottleneck to growth.

Huge cloud providers continue to pour tens of billions of dollars into data centers, fueling the AI infrastructure boom, and Broadcom (AVGO-US), which designs custom AI chips for tech giants, is one of the main beneficiaries. According to its financials, Broadcom’s AI semiconductor business has generated about $68 billion in cumulative revenue since the end of 2023. In the third quarter of its fiscal 2026 year ending August 2, 2026, AI semiconductor revenue more than doubled year‑over‑year to $16.7 billion, more than three times the same period a year earlier.

However, Broadcom’s rapid growth does not mean the entire AI supply chain can profit smoothly. Bloomberg reported that Broadcom CEO Chen Fu-yang said at DBS Bank’s Asia Future Outlook conference in Singapore last week that many investors know “absolutely nothing” about what they are backing yet hold sky‑high expectations, and may end up feeling “as if they are in a casino.”

Broadcom supplies the hardware that top AI labs need to build compute systems, allowing it to benefit directly from chip sales and related product demand. But for AI labs that purchase massive compute resources, the challenge is finding enough paying customers to cover the huge costs of model development, training and day‑to‑day operations.

Chen pointed out that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was reported at $50 billion as of the end of September, showing that frontier AI models indeed have huge commercial potential. However, annualized revenue is a projection based on current revenue pace, not the actual amount earned over the past 12 months, and it cannot be taken as profit.

He added that OpenAI is still loss‑making because it continues to pour large sums into model training. He believes current data only show that cutting‑edge generative AI models have significant revenue growth potential, but that does not yet prove that the companies have built long‑term profitable business models. OpenAI expects model‑training expenses alone to exceed $25 billion this year, indicating that even rapid revenue expansion may be eroded by high compute and R&D costs.

Another hidden risk for the AI industry is whether capital will keep flowing. As investment in AI data centers, chips and compute infrastructure keeps climbing, some analysts expect AI capital‑expenditure growth to slow next year. Chen argues that, compared with shortages of memory, semiconductors or power, a funding shortfall “may be the biggest constraint on the AI industry.”

The market is already showing signs that investors are reassessing financing needs for AI infrastructure. Bloomberg reported that Firmus, an Australian data‑center operator backed by NVIDIA (NVDA‑US), had planned an IPO but withdrew the filing on October 9 after weak demand for the proposed price, reflecting a cautious stance on valuations and financing conditions for AI infrastructure firms and underscoring that even a rosy industry outlook requires sufficient capital for expansion.

Nevertheless, a more cautious financing environment does not mean AI compute demand has cooled. Intel (INTC‑US) CEO Pat Gelsinger said at the same conference that, according to Bloomberg, hardware supply shortages could persist for two to three more years. This suggests chip and related equipment demand may stay strong, but strong demand and corporate profitability are separate issues. If AI firms cannot turn rising infrastructure spend into enough paying demand, more chips in the market does not guarantee sensible investment.

Beyond pressure on AI model developers, Chen also criticized how corporate customers use AI. He noted many firms spend money buying tokens for various AI experiments without first confirming which applications truly improve operational efficiency or deliver financial returns, leading to continuous cash burn without corresponding value creation.

He likened it to his childhood experience of spending a $10 token bundle at an arcade, watching it disappear in ten minutes with nothing to show for it. Chen warned that if companies keep pouring money into AI just to keep up with the trend, without clear use‑case goals and performance metrics, they will merely add costs rather than boost productivity or profitability.

The concern echoes a McKinsey survey released in August on AI investment returns. The survey found 80% of respondents say AI has improved personal work efficiency, but only 37% say AI has positively contributed to their organization’s EBIT. About one‑fifth of respondents said AI‑related operating costs, including token expenses, are limiting further adoption.

Overall, the AI industry faces a gap between growing demand and commercial returns. From Broadcom’s soaring AI semiconductor revenue, to AI labs shouldering high training costs, to corporate customers still struggling to turn AI into profit, the market must assess not only how long chip demand can grow but also whether companies can build sustainable revenue streams and whether investors will keep funding massive capital outlays. For AI, the real test is not just building bigger models and compute systems, but converting technological demand into long‑term, measurable, cost‑covering business value.
